conventions.convention: Singular cohomology uses the positive coboundary delta(phi) = phi composed with the boundary (no degree sign), and the cup product is the front/back-face formula (phi cup psi)(sigma) = phi(sigma[0..p]) * psi(sigma[p..p+q]) with no extra cochain sign.
Cap product is written cohomology-first: evaluate on the front p-face and retain the back (n-p)-face, with the boundary identity partial(phi cap c) = (-1)^p (phi cap partial c - delta phi cap c).

Relative cup and cap products are constructed only for two subspaces open in their union, or for a supplied pair whose quotient-chain comparison is separately proved; the relative cup target is H^{p+q}(X,U) reached through that canonical quotient-cochain isomorphism.

Manifold means Hausdorff with an at-most-countable basis and half-space charts; the boundary is the set of points sent to the model boundary by some chart, the model boundary of the zero-dimensional model is empty, and all chart choices are individual existential hypotheses.

An R-orientation is a continuous section of the orientation local system whose values generate each stalk as an R-module (the system topology being fixed by coordinate-ball sections); for a manifold with boundary it orients the interior only.

Boundary orientation is outward-normal-first: in n-1 tangential coordinates followed by an inward collar coordinate the induced boundary generator is (-1)^n times the tangential generator, and the pair fundamental class restricts to the boundary fundamental class.

The standard affine k-simplex carries the ordered-basis orientation with boundary sum_i (-1)^i face_i and the zero-simplex positive; integration over a smooth singular simplex is the oriented coordinate integral of the pulled-back form, equal to point evaluation in degree zero.

De Rham cohomology of a manifold with boundary is the cohomology of forms whose boundary-chart coefficients are locally extendible; the global de Rham comparison (vector-space and ring form) assumes only countable choice, entering through form partitions and the countable Mayer-Vietoris/product arguments.

On an oriented boundaryless manifold the integral of compactly supported top forms is the choice-free finite-localization integral, H_c^n uses compactly supported primitives, and the degree of a proper smooth map is the unique scalar with integral(F^* omega) = deg(F) integral(omega).

Degree of a map between nonempty connected closed integrally oriented manifolds is the unique integer with f_*[M] = deg(f)[N]; the local orientation sign of a regular preimage compares determinant-line rays (the product of the two point signs in dimension zero).

Throughout the geodesics page we assume the boundaryless convention: manifolds have empty boundary, a geodesic is affinely parametrized unless stated otherwise, energy carries the factor 1/2, and the geodesic spray, exponential map, normal neighbourhoods and Hopf-Rinow are developed under countable choice.

The exponential domain is E = {v in TM : 1 lies in I_{pi(v),v}} (time-one evaluation of the unique maximal geodesic); normal coordinates require a star-shaped open tangent domain carried diffeomorphically by exp_p; the injectivity radius at p is the supremum of admissible radii and the empty manifold has injectivity radius +infinity.

The Hurewicz homomorphism uses a fixed positive sphere generator in the absolute case and, for n at least 2, the unique relative disk class whose homology boundary is the positive sphere generator; the relative homomorphism is not defined in degree one.

A CW pair (X,A) is k-connected when every path component of X meets A and every relative pi_i(X,A,a), 1 <= i <= k, is trivial at every a in A (relative degree one is a pointed set and relative pi_0 is not defined); equivalently every disk (D^i,S^{i-1}) -> (X,A) with i <= k compresses into A with its whole boundary fixed.
A weak homotopy equivalence is a map inducing a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on pi_n at every source basepoint, for arbitrary topological spaces with no CW or separation hypothesis.

Cup length counts only positive-degree classes, is 0 when no nonzero finite positive-degree product exists and infinity when the admissible lengths are unbounded; no cup length is assigned to the empty space.

Cellular approximation, the source-compression lemma and Whitehead are stated in two clauses: choice-free when only finitely many relative cells are involved and under AC in general, and this choice boundary is inherited by every item that extends them to arbitrary cell sets.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold M with boundary, if Omega^k(M) consists of forms whose boundary-chart coefficients are locally restrictions of smooth Euclidean functions, then the local formula d(sum_I f_I dx^I) = sum_I df_I wedge dx^I defines an extension-independent smooth form independent of the chart, real linear, satisfying the graded Leibniz rule and d^2 = 0, commuting with pullback by every smooth map between manifolds with boundary; (Omega^*(M),d) is a real cochain complex.

Assume AC_omega. For every (p,v) in TM there is a unique maximal geodesic gamma_{p,v}: I_{p,v} -> M with gamma_{p,v}(0) = p and gamma'_{p,v}(0) = v; each I_{p,v} is an open interval containing zero, the domain G = {(t,p,v) : t in I_{p,v}} is open in R x TM, and (t,p,v) maps to gamma_{p,v}(t) smoothly on G.

In coordinates x^1,...,x^n, a smooth curve gamma is a geodesic if and only if, throughout every parameter subinterval lying in the chart, x-double-dot^k + Gamma^k_{ij}(x) x-dot^i x-dot^j = 0 for every k, with summation over repeated indices.

For p,q >= 0 and cochains phi in C^p(X;R), psi in C^q(X;R) over a commutative unital ring R, with the positive coboundary delta phi = phi partial, the cup product is (phi cup psi)(sigma) = phi(sigma[0,...,p]) psi(sigma[p,...,p+q]) for sigma : Delta^{p+q} -> X, extended R-linearly; zero or negative-degree inputs give zero.

Assume AC_omega; let (M,g) be a nonempty connected boundaryless Riemannian manifold with Riemannian distance d. The following are equivalent: (1) (M,d) is complete; (2) (M,g) is geodesically complete; (3) E_p = T_pM for every p; (4) E_{p_0} = T_{p_0}M for some point p_0; (5) every closed bounded subset of (M,d) is compact. Whenever these hold, every x,y are joined by a minimizing geodesic, namely exp_x(v) = y with |v| = d(x,y).

A continuous map f : X -> Y is a weak homotopy equivalence when the function pi_0(f) : pi_0(X) -> pi_0(Y) is bijective and, for every x in X and every integer n >= 1, the homomorphism f_* : pi_n(X,x) -> pi_n(Y,f(x)) is an isomorphism; the quantifiers include every component and every source basepoint.

Let K be a compact topological space and f : K -> X continuous, where X is a CW complex with its characteristic maps supplied as part of the structure. Then f(K) lies in a finite CW subcomplex of X, with no AC or countable choice used, even when the cells of X form an arbitrary set and their dimensions are unbounded.

Attaching to a CW complex A a set of zero-cells and, in ascending dimension, sets of k-disks whose attaching images meet finitely many cells yields a CW complex Z with the weak attachment topology, with the old spaces as closed subcomplexes and with the characteristic-disk continuity test, using no choice principle.

Fix positive orientation generators [S^n] in H_n(S^n;Z) for n >= 1. The absolute Hurewicz homomorphism is h([f]) = f_*[S^n]; for n >= 2 the relative Hurewicz homomorphism is h([f]) = f_*[D^n,S^{n-1}], where [D^n,S^{n-1}] is the unique class whose homology boundary is the positive boundary-sphere generator.

For continuous f : X -> Y and a commutative unital ring R, f^*(a cup b) = f^*a cup f^*b and f^*(1) = 1; cup product is associative already on cochains, so f^* : H^*(Y;R) -> H^*(X;R) is a unital graded-ring homomorphism, and homotopic maps give the same homomorphism.

For a compact boundaryless n-manifold M with a specified R-orientation mu, its fundamental class is [M] = [M]_M in H_n(M, M setminus M;R) = H_n(M;R), the class proved to exist uniquely with point restriction mu_x at every x in M.

For a locally compact Hausdorff space X, H_c^p(X;G) is the colimit of the relative groups H^p(X, X setminus K;G) over compact K, with transitions induced by inclusions of relative cochain complexes and an explicit common-larger-support equality relation; the construction is choice-free.

Assume AC_omega. A Riemannian manifold without boundary is geodesically complete when for every initial vector v in T_pM the unique maximal geodesic has domain I_{p,v} = R; for a disconnected manifold the condition is componentwise and the zero initial vector is included.

For a boundaryless n-manifold M, R commutative unital and K compact: H_i(M, M setminus K;R) = 0 for i > n, restriction in degree n to all point stalks over K is injective, and every continuous section of the local R-homology system is realized by a unique class in the relative group; in particular an R-orientation determines a unique [M]_K restricting to its generator at each point of K, compatibly with inclusions and splitting over the finitely many components meeting K.

A CW pair (X,A) is k-connected when every path component of X meets A and, for every a in A and every 1 <= i <= k, the pointed set or group pi_i(X,A,a) has one element; equivalently every continuous (D^i,S^{i-1}) -> (X,A) with i <= k is homotopic into A while its whole boundary is fixed.

For phi in C^p(X;R), c in C_n(X;R) and p,n >= 0 over a commutative unital ring, partial(phi cap c) = (-1)^p (phi cap partial c - delta phi cap c); consequently cap induces an R-bilinear map H^p(X;R) tensor H_n(X;R) -> H_{n-p}(X;R), with no AC assumed.

Let F : M^n -> N^n be proper and smooth with M,N nonempty connected oriented boundaryless smooth manifolds. Its degree is the scalar Int_M composed with F_c^* composed with Int_N^{-1} of 1, equivalently the unique scalar with integral_M F^*omega = deg(F) integral_N omega for every compactly supported top form omega; the integration isomorphisms use the choice-free finite-localization integral.

concerns.concern: The Verification reproduces, step for step (1.1 through 8.1), the entire proof of lem-integral-surface-cup-pairing-from-the-oriented-polygon: same statement, same genus-g polygon, same fan/triangles, same cup recurrence and same signs. As a B-page example of an A-page lemma it adds no illustration of its own and duplicates roughly a thousand words; the two items should be reconciled (example = illustration, lemma = proof) or cross-referenced.

This theorem assumes AC, but the same page contains lem-relative-hurewicz-comparison-through-a-choice-free-weak-model, which proves the identical conclusion (H_i(X,A;Z) = 0 for 0 <= i < n and h : pi_n(X,A,a) -> H_n(X,A;Z) an isomorphism for an (n-1)-connected CW pair with A nonempty simply connected, n >= 2) with no choice principle at all; thm-absolute-hurewicz-theorem then inherits the unnecessary AC hypothesis through this item. The AC flag is sound as bookkeeping for the quoted replacement argument but overstates what the group needs; adjudication should decide which statement is canonical and whether the absolute theorem can drop AC.

Step 1.2 proves the stronger statement that no unital multiplication on Z^2 can be invariant under every additive automorphism, whereas the refuted claim only says a bare abelian group does not determine a unital multiplication without extra data. The load-bearing witness is the explicit pair of unital rings Z x Z and Z[epsilon]/(epsilon^2) on the same additive group in steps 1.1 and 3.1; the invariance argument is extra and its phrase no unital multiplication can be recovered could be misread as denying all canonical constructions, which is not what the counterexample needs.

Step 6.2 asserts continuity of the homotopy-extension retraction at the collar limit by prose alone: as v approaches b from below, a(v) = v/(b-v) tends to infinity, uniformly dominating t in [0,1], and the new collar height tends to b, so the formula extends continuously to the outside rule. The necessary uniform estimate (both branches approaching the same limit value, including the piecewise-defined second branch and the r=0 case) is not displayed, so a reader must reconstruct an epsilon computation to certify the stated HEP retraction.
